faq.org: Water ice a few centimetres down, perchlorates in the soil and snowfall detected by LIDAR.

marte-curiosity.casi_fallo: It landed hanging from a flying crane never tested on Mars: 7 minutes in which everything had to go right with no help from Earth.
marte-curiosity.leccion: Wheels wear out more than expected on sharp rock; routes have to be planned and designs made for the real terrain.
marte-curiosity.logro: It showed that Gale crater once held a habitable lake and it has been active since 2012.
marte-curiosity.por_que_termino: It is still active on the Martian surface.
marte-curiosity.radiactivo_detalle: MMRTG with 4.8 kg of plutonium-238 dioxide

texto.ninos: This robot weighs almost 900 kilos, like a car, and came down to Mars hanging from a flying crane. Its wheels are leaving little bits of metal along the way. What would you ask it if you could call it?
texto.org: Curiosity (MSL), landing on Aug 6, 2012 at 4.59 S, 137.44 E (Gale crater) by sky crane; active, powered by an MMRTG with 4.8 kg of PuO2. Its wheels have shed aluminium fragments along the route (Kilic 2022). Coordinates: PDS Geosciences Node.

faq.ninos: Yes. It has spent more than 13 years climbing a mountain inside a crater.
faq.org: Active since 2012; it is climbing Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons). Its generator is gradually losing power, which limits daily operations.

faq.ninos: A little: tiny bits of its wheels and the parts from its landing. Scientists log every one.
faq.org: EDL hardware (heat shield, parachute, sky crane) scattered near the site and aluminium fragments from the wheels; they are documented so they are not mistaken for samples (Kilic 2022).

marte-schiaparelli.objeto: Entry, descent and landing demonstrator module (EDM)
marte-schiaparelli.casi_fallo: A rotation sensor saturated for one second; the software calculated that it was already below the ground, released the parachute and shut the engines off 3.7 km up.
marte-schiaparelli.leccion: Software must distrust impossible data; one second of bad readings cannot decide the landing.
marte-schiaparelli.logro: It transmitted entry and descent data that fed the design of later European landings.
marte-schiaparelli.por_que_termino: It crashed during descent or landing.
marte-schiaparelli.nota: No coordinates in the source: 'near the Opportunity site'.

texto.ninos: This spacecraft believed it had reached the ground when it was still almost 4 kilometres up, higher than ten Eiffel Towers. It shut off its engines and fell. What would you have told it one second earlier?
texto.org: Schiaparelli EDM (ESA), impact on Oct 19, 2016 at ~2.07 S, 6.21 W (Meridiani Planum) at ~540 km/h; IMU saturation led to a calculated negative altitude and premature shutdown. Approximate coordinates (MRO images), not checked against a primary source; status: Kilic 2022 (crashed spacecraft).

faq.ninos: Yes, in pieces. It left a dark smudge that was seen from orbit the next day.
faq.org: Impact crater and debris (parachute, heat shield) photographed by MRO's HiRISE a few days later, near the Opportunity site.

faq.ninos: Yes: it sent data on the way down, and that is how they learned what to fix.
faq.org: EDL telemetry was received in full up to impact; ESA's investigation (2017) identified the cause and fed into the design of the Kazachok platform.

marte-insight.estado: Inactive (panels covered in dust, end of mission in December 2022)
marte-insight.casi_fallo: Its heat probe never managed to bury itself: the soil did not grip as expected. Dust gradually covered the panels until it ran out of power.
marte-insight.leccion: The soil of another planet can behave differently from anything tested on Earth.
marte-insight.logro: First seismometer on Mars: it recorded more than 1,300 quakes and measured the size of the planet's core.
marte-insight.por_que_termino: It was left inactive on the Martian surface.
marte-insight.historia: It deployed an ultra-sensitive seismometer on a quiet plain in Elysium Planitia to listen to the planet's interior.
marte-insight.legado_cientifico: It recorded more than a thousand 'marsquakes', and made it possible to estimate the thickness of the crust and the size of the core and to detect meteorite impacts.
marte-insight.equipo_dejado: Fixed platform with circular solar panels, the SEIS seismometer under its protective dome and the HP3 heat probe.

texto.ninos: This spacecraft put an ear to the ground on Mars and heard more than 1,300 quakes, almost one a day for 4 years. Dust covered its panels and it shut down. What does a quake sound like on Mars?
texto.org: InSight, landing on Nov 26, 2018 at 4.502 N, 135.623 E (Elysium Planitia); the SEIS seismometer recorded >1,300 quakes. End of mission on Dec 21, 2022 due to dust build-up on the panels. Coordinates: Lakdawalla's map, The Planetary Society.

faq.ninos: Yes, motionless and covered in dust, with its ear still pressed to the ground.
faq.org: Inactive since Dec 2022; the lander, the deployed seismometer and the HP3 probe remain in Elysium Planitia.

faq.ninos: That Mars has a heart of liquid metal and that it still shakes.
faq.org: It determined the radius of the core (~1,830 km) and the structure of the crust and mantle from seismic waves; it detected meteorite impacts as seismic sources.

marte-perseverance.casi_fallo: It landed in a crater full of cliffs and dunes, the hardest site chosen up to then, guiding itself with its cameras alone.
marte-perseverance.leccion: Even its own debris gets documented: in 2022 it found netting from its landing and logged it so as not to contaminate its samples.
marte-perseverance.logro: It collects rock samples to bring them to Earth and took the first helicopter to another planet.
marte-perseverance.por_que_termino: Perseverance is still active; Ingenuity was left immobile in Jezero crater after a rotor was damaged in January 2024.
marte-perseverance.nota: Coordinates of the landing target from the site-selection workshop, not the final position.
marte-perseverance.historia: It travelled attached to the Perseverance rover and made 72 flights in the thin atmosphere of Mars, far exceeding its 5 planned flights.
marte-perseverance.legado_cientifico: It showed that powered, controlled flight is feasible on other worlds, opening the era of planetary aerial exploration.
marte-perseverance.equipo_dejado: Carbon-fibre body, two counter-rotating coaxial rotors and a solar panel on top, in Jezero crater.
marte-perseverance.radiactivo_detalle: MMRTG with 4.8 kg of plutonium-238 dioxide

texto.ninos: This robot weighs one tonne, like a baby hippo, and stores Mars rocks in tubes to bring them back one day. In 2022 it found a tangled net that had fallen from its own landing. What did it think when it saw it?
texto.org: Perseverance (Mars 2020), landing on Feb 18, 2021 at 18.4447 N, 77.4508 E (Jezero crater); active, MMRTG with 4.8 kg of PuO2. It found netting debris from its descent system on Jul 12, 2022 (Kilic 2022). Lakdawalla's map shows the centre of the planned ellipse (18.3628 N, 77.5945 E); the coordinates here are those of the actual landing.

faq.ninos: Yes. It is roaming the crater and has already left tubes with samples on the ground.
faq.org: Active since 2021; it has laid down a sample-tube depot at Three Forks and is exploring the rim of Jezero.

faq.ninos: Only a tiny bit. It was cleaned so thoroughly that its microbes would not even cover a phone camera lens. And no person has ever been to Mars.
faq.org: Planetary protection: the whole Mars 2020 spacecraft carried fewer than 500,000 spores, the landed parts up to 300,000 and the rover 41,000 (NASA JPL). No human has been on Mars.

marte-ingenuity.estado: Inactive (rotor damaged after flight 72; retired in January 2024)
marte-ingenuity.casi_fallo: It was meant to make 5 test flights; on flight 72 it landed on smooth, featureless sand, became disoriented and broke a rotor blade.
marte-ingenuity.leccion: Terrain with no landmarks confuses the navigation camera; even a huge success ends because of a small detail.
marte-ingenuity.logro: First powered flight on another planet (Apr 19, 2021); 72 flights instead of the 5 planned.
marte-ingenuity.historia: It travelled attached to the Perseverance rover and made 72 flights in the thin atmosphere of Mars, far exceeding its 5 planned flights.
marte-ingenuity.legado_cientifico: It showed that powered, controlled flight is feasible on other worlds, opening the era of planetary aerial exploration.
marte-ingenuity.equipo_dejado: Carbon-fibre body, two counter-rotating coaxial rotors and a solar panel on top, in Jezero crater.

texto.ninos: This helicopter weighs less than 2 kilos, like a big bottle of water, and was the first to fly on another planet. It flew 72 times until one of its wings broke. Where would you fly on Mars?
texto.org: Ingenuity (Mars 2020), arrived under Perseverance on Feb 18, 2021; first flight on Apr 19, 2021 and last (no. 72) on Jan 18, 2024, with rotor blade damage in Neretva Vallis. Approximate final position ~18.5 N, 77.4 E, not checked against a primary source.

faq.ninos: Yes, standing in the sand with a broken wing. Perseverance took one last photo of it from afar.
faq.org: Inactive since Jan 2024 due to blade damage; it remains in Neretva Vallis, inside Jezero, photographed by Perseverance.

faq.ninos: It showed that you can fly in very thin air. Now bigger helicopters are being planned.
faq.org: Technology demonstration of flight in an atmosphere ~1% the density of Earth's; the basis for future Mars scout helicopters.

espacio-profundo-pioneer-10.objeto: Interplanetary probe with a message plaque
espacio-profundo-pioneer-10.casi_fallo: It crossed the asteroid belt and Jupiter's radiation, which almost damaged its instruments.
espacio-profundo-pioneer-10.leccion: Its power source degraded until it could no longer transmit; power limits the life of a mission.
espacio-profundo-pioneer-10.logro: First spacecraft to reach Jupiter and to leave the inner solar system; it carries a plaque with a message from humanity.
espacio-profundo-pioneer-10.por_que_termino: Its radioisotope power source degraded and the signal dropped below the detection threshold.
espacio-profundo-pioneer-10.nota: Travelling towards interstellar space, in the general direction of the star Aldebaran (Taurus)
espacio-profundo-pioneer-10.donde_esta: Travelling towards interstellar space, in the general direction of the star Aldebaran (Taurus)
espacio-profundo-pioneer-10.ubicacion: Heading for Aldebaran (Taurus); it will take more than 2 million years

texto.ninos: This probe was the first to visit Jupiter and is still travelling towards a distant star. It carries a plaque with a drawing of two people and will take more than 2 million years to arrive, longer than all of human history. What would you draw on that plaque?
texto.org: Pioneer 10 (1972-012A), launched on Mar 3, 1972; Jupiter flyby in Dec 1973. Last signal received on Jan 23, 2003 due to degradation of the SNAP-19 RTGs. Hyperbolic trajectory towards Aldebaran. Source: NASA.

faq.ninos: Very far away, beyond Pluto, travelling in silence.
faq.org: More than 130 AU from the Sun, receding at ~12 km/s; position in JPL Horizons.

faq.ninos: Yes, it carries batteries that run on the heat of a radioactive material.
faq.org: Four SNAP-19 RTGs with Pu-238 (NASA RPS); their power decayed until transmission became impossible.

espacio-profundo-pioneer-11.objeto: Interplanetary probe with a message plaque
espacio-profundo-pioneer-11.casi_fallo: It passed just 43,000 km from Jupiter's clouds, three times closer than Pioneer 10, at risk of radiation damage.
espacio-profundo-pioneer-11.leccion: Earth moved out of its antenna's field and contact was lost; a spacecraft with no power to orient itself falls silent.
espacio-profundo-pioneer-11.logro: First spacecraft to fly past Saturn and its rings (1979).
espacio-profundo-pioneer-11.por_que_termino: Earth moved out of its antenna's field of view and it cannot be reoriented.
espacio-profundo-pioneer-11.nota: Travelling towards the constellation Aquila (the Eagle)
espacio-profundo-pioneer-11.donde_esta: Travelling towards the constellation Aquila (the Eagle)

texto.ninos: This probe was the first to see Saturn's rings up close. Today it travels silently towards the constellation of the Eagle, at more than 15 kilometres per second, a hundred times faster than a plane. What will it see on the way?
texto.org: Pioneer 11 (1973-019A), launched on Apr 6, 1973; flybys of Jupiter (1974) and Saturn (1979). Last contact on Sep 30, 1995 when Earth moved out of its antenna beam. Escape trajectory towards Aquila. Source: NASA.

faq.ninos: Far from the Sun, heading the opposite way from its sister Pioneer 10.
faq.org: More than 100 AU from the Sun; position in JPL Horizons.

faq.ninos: Yes, it carries radioactive heat batteries like its sister.
faq.org: Four SNAP-19 RTGs with Pu-238 (NASA RPS).

espacio-profundo-near-shoemaker.casi_fallo: In 1998 an aborted burn made it miss its first appointment with Eros; it took one more year to arrive.
espacio-profundo-near-shoemaker.leccion: Extreme cold shut it down two weeks after landing; a plan B (landing without being designed for it) yielded extra science.
espacio-profundo-near-shoemaker.logro: First spacecraft to orbit and to land on an asteroid.
espacio-profundo-near-shoemaker.por_que_termino: After landing it kept transmitting; the extreme cold finished it off.
espacio-profundo-near-shoemaker.nota: On the surface of asteroid 433 Eros
espacio-profundo-near-shoemaker.donde_esta: On the surface of asteroid 433 Eros
espacio-profundo-near-shoemaker.ubicacion: On the surface of asteroid 433 Eros

texto.ninos: This spacecraft was not built to land, but at the end of its mission it set down gently on an asteroid 34 kilometres long, like a whole city floating in space. How would it feel to touch an asteroid?
texto.org: NEAR Shoemaker (1996-008A), launched on Feb 17, 1996; in orbit around 433 Eros from Feb 14, 2000 and landing on Feb 12, 2001. Last contact on Feb 28, 2001 because of the extreme cold. Source: NASA.

faq.ninos: Yes, it rests on asteroid Eros, which circles the Sun.
faq.org: It remains on the surface of Eros; no contact since Feb 28, 2001.

faq.ninos: It was too cold and it shut down.
faq.org: Temperatures below the operating limit after landing; mission closed two weeks later.

espacio-profundo-dawn.casi_fallo: It lost two of its four reaction wheels and had to orient itself with hydrazine thrusters.
espacio-profundo-dawn.leccion: The hydrazine for pointing ran out; without attitude control it cannot aim its antenna or its panels.
espacio-profundo-dawn.logro: First spacecraft to orbit two destinations beyond Earth (Vesta and Ceres) and to visit a dwarf planet.
espacio-profundo-dawn.por_que_termino: It ran out of the hydrazine it used to point its antennas at Earth and its panels at the Sun.
espacio-profundo-dawn.nota: In orbit around the dwarf planet Ceres (with no power to orient itself)
espacio-profundo-dawn.donde_esta: In orbit around the dwarf planet Ceres (with no power to orient itself)

texto.ninos: This spacecraft visited two worlds in the asteroid belt with an engine that pushes very gently, like the weight of a sheet of paper, but for years. It ran out of fuel and now circles Ceres in silence. How far would you get with such a gentle push?
texto.org: Dawn (2007-043A), launched on Sep 27, 2007; it orbited Vesta (2011-2012) and Ceres (from 2015). End of mission announced on Nov 1, 2018 when the hydrazine ran out. It remains in a stable orbit around Ceres for planetary protection (at least 20 years). Source: NASA JPL.

faq.ninos: Yes, it circles Ceres like a small artificial moon.
faq.org: In orbit around Ceres; the orbit was designed not to impact for at least 20 years (planetary protection).

faq.ninos: So as not to dirty Ceres, which could have water and is interesting in the search for life.
faq.org: Ceres is a body of astrobiological interest (planetary protection category); contamination was avoided.

espacio-profundo-kepler.casi_fallo: Two of its four reaction wheels failed in 2012 and 2013; it looked like the end, but engineers used the pressure of sunlight to balance it (K2 mission).
espacio-profundo-kepler.leccion: Without fuel it cannot point; it was retired with dignity and its data is still being analysed.
espacio-profundo-kepler.logro: More than 2,600 confirmed exoplanets: it showed that there are more planets than stars in the galaxy.
espacio-profundo-kepler.por_que_termino: It ran out of fuel after about 9 years of a mission planned for 3.5.
espacio-profundo-kepler.nota: In orbit around the Sun, trailing Earth ('Earth-trailing' orbit), far from us
espacio-profundo-kepler.donde_esta: In orbit around the Sun, trailing Earth ('Earth-trailing' orbit), far from us
espacio-profundo-kepler.ubicacion: In orbit around the Sun, behind Earth

texto.ninos: This telescope discovered more than 2,600 planets around other stars, more than all those known before put together. It ran out of fuel and now trails Earth silently around the Sun. What would a planet discovered by you be like?
texto.org: Kepler (2009-011A), launched on Mar 7, 2009 into an Earth-trailing heliocentric orbit. Retired on Oct 30, 2018 when its fuel ran out; final commands on Nov 15, 2018. More than 2,600 confirmed exoplanets. Source: NASA.

faq.ninos: Trailing Earth around the Sun, a little further behind each time.
faq.org: Earth-trailing heliocentric orbit; it drifts away from Earth by about 0.1 AU per year.

faq.pregunta: Is it still of any use?
faq.ninos: Yes: its stored photos keep yielding new discoveries.
faq.org: The data archive keeps producing detections and is the basis for missions such as TESS.
